topic: State Executive: Governor and Chief Minister
description: Part VI of the Indian Constitution (Articles 153 to 167) deals with the State Executive. The state executive consists of the Governor, the Chief Minister, the Council of Ministers, and the Advocate General of the State.

sections.title: Office and Appointment of the Governor
sections.description: The Governor acts as the constitutional head of the state as well as a representative of the Central Government.

key_concepts.explanation: The Governor is the nominal executive head of the state, while the real executive powers are vested in the Chief Minister.
Although the normal term of a Governor is 5 years, they hold office subject to the pleasure of the President and can be removed at any time.

polity_articles.provision: There shall be a Governor for each state.
polity_articles.details: The 7th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1956 facilitated the appointment of the same person as a governor for two or more states.
The Governor is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal (based on the Canadian Model).
The person must be a citizen of India and must have completed 35 years of age.

important_facts.fact: The oath of office to the Governor is administered by the Chief Justice of the concerned State High Court (or in their absence, the senior-most judge of that court).

sections.title: Powers and Functions of the Governor
sections.description: The Governor possesses executive, legislative, financial, and judicial powers, but lacks military or diplomatic powers.

key_concepts.explanation: The Constitution empowers the Governor to act without the advice of the Council of Ministers in specific situations, such as recommending President's Rule or reserving a bill for the President's consideration.

polity_articles.details: The Governor can pardon, reprieve, respite, or remit punishments for offenses against state laws, but cannot pardon a death sentence or a court-martial sentence.
The Governor can give assent, withhold assent, return the bill (if not a money bill), or reserve the bill for the consideration of the President.
The Governor can issue ordinances when the State Legislature is not in session. These must be approved by the state legislature within 6 weeks of its reassembly.

important_facts.fact: The Contingency Fund of the State is at the disposal of the Governor to make advances to meet unforeseen expenditure pending its authorization by the state legislature.

sections.title: Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
sections.description: The Chief Minister is the real executive (de facto) head of the state government and plays a pivotal role in shaping state policies.

key_concepts.explanation: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the State Legislative Assembly. If a no-confidence motion is passed, all ministers must resign.

polity_articles.provision: Council of Ministers to aid and advise the Governor.
polity_articles.details: Except in matters where the Governor acts in their discretion, they shall act on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister.
The Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor, and other ministers are appointed by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister.

polity_articles.provision: Limiting the size of the Council of Ministers.
polity_articles.details: The total number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, in a state shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly (minimum of 12 ministers).

key_associations.extra_info: The Chief Minister acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the State Planning Board.
The Chief Minister is a member of these councils, both of which are headed by the Prime Minister.

sections.title: Relationship between Governor and Chief Minister
sections.description: The Chief Minister acts as the principal channel of communication between the Governor and the Council of Ministers.

polity_articles.provision: Duties of Chief Minister regarding furnishing of information to the Governor.
polity_articles.details: It is the duty of the CM to communicate to the Governor all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to state administration and legislative proposals.

important_facts.fact: If the Governor requires, the Chief Minister must submit for the consideration of the Council of Ministers any matter on which a decision has been taken by a minister but which has not been considered by the council.
